New junior member Dennis Gleeson ran very well to take 1st spot in the senior 100y,and then dashed straight back to the start to get on his marks for the junior race where he again thrashed the opposition.

…al Ash, had no difficulty in winning the Discus after already competing in two other events.New members Frank Glass and Dennis Gleeson also performed well,the latter looking as if he could well be a member of our winning team in the AAA Champs 4x110y 1966-1970.…

For those who are are not 'au fait' with the team,the regular members are:- Jim Vivian,Chris Martin,Denis Gleeson and Clive Oliver. Other juniors who have had a good season are John Mitchell,John Martin, Phil Smith,Bob Nelson,Dave Nicklin and Adrian Major.
In the absence of Jim Vivian (just out of hospital after an appendicitis operation) the Belgrave flag was still kept flying in the sprints with good efforts by Chris Martin and Denis Gleeson.

Denis Gleeson enjoyed himself in the pouring rain by taking all three sprints,his 'quarter' being exceptionally good. This was only his second try at the distance and running virtually on his own he recorded 52.4 .

After finishing 3rd in the 'A' 100 yds, Denis Gleeson was a convincing winner of the 'A' 440 yds, clocking 52.4. Jim Vivian was an easy winner of the'A' 220 yds (23.1) whilst John Mitchell clocked a very sharp 10.3 in the 'B' 100 yds.
Ben Lulham's 'stable' was well to the forefront in the absence of Jim Vivian (appendicitis) both 100y and 220y were won by Chris Martin with Denis Gleeson and C.Oliver second and third in both races.
Stimpson, the award of Junior Honours Badges to J.Vivian J. Martin, D.

After taking up the 'quarter' only halfway through the season, Denis Gleeson now has a best time of 51.3. With a little extra strength gained during this winter, next season should see him under 50.0 and providing the nucleus of a decent Senior 4 x 440y team.
With brilliant baton passing, Denis Gleeson and Chris Martin put us even further ahead and when Jim Vivian took the baton for the last leg it was all over.
